ov: The most widespread wild cat, a spotted, secretive hunter that survives almost anywhere with cover: rainforest, savanna, mountains and semi-desert across Africa and Asia.

why.dg: Some became man-eaters: the Leopard of Rudraprayag killed more than 125 people.
why.ac: Mainly active from dusk to dawn, resting through most of the day.

wt: 20–72 kg; big males up to 91 kg
rg: Much of sub-Saharan Africa, with fragmented, declining populations across the Middle East, South and Southeast Asia, China and the Russian Far East.
df: Almost anything it can overpower, from antelope and deer to monkeys, rodents and birds. Kills are often dragged up a tree.

cf.tip: A jaguar is stockier with a bigger head, and its rosettes are larger, often with a spot inside. Jaguars live only in the Americas; leopards only in Africa and Asia.
A cheetah has solid round spots rather than rosettes, black “tear” lines from eye to mouth, and a slimmer, longer-legged build.
